facts.raw_span: A patient with high myopia was examined
The axial length was 30.0 mm
a yellowish oval lesion within a wide area of chorioretinal atrophy
a ringlike low reflectance pattern
a focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina
The sclera was approximately one-third thinner
98, 77, and 50 μm for the pit's floor, temporal wall, and nasal wall, respectively
The choroid was obliterated
Width and depth of 522 × 536 μm
The pit had a homogeneous low autofluorescence
Showed a branch of a posterior ciliary artery near the lesion
The pit was slightly hyperfluorescent in the late frames

concepts.why: High myopia and chorioretinal atrophy are characteristic of pathologic myopia.
Focal scleral ectasia and thinning are consistent with scleral ectasia.
Chorioretinal atrophy and obliterated choroid are indicative of choroidal atrophy.
The presence of a branch of a posterior ciliary artery near the lesion suggests an anomaly.
High myopia and retinal degeneration are characteristic of myopic retinal degeneration.
Focal scleral ectasia and thinning are consistent with scleral staphyloma.
Chorioretinal atrophy and low autofluorescence are indicative of chorioretinal scarring.
High myopia and macular degeneration are characteristic of myopic maculopathy.
The ringlike low reflectance pattern in infrared examination is explained by scleral ectasia with choroidal obliteration.

rationales.F01: High myopia is a risk factor for pathologic myopia and myopic retinal degeneration.
rationales.F02: Axial length of 30.0 mm is highly suggestive of pathologic myopia and scleral ectasia.
rationales.F03: The presence of a yellowish oval lesion within a wide area of chorioretinal atrophy is consistent with pathologic myopia and choroidal atrophy.
rationales.F05: Focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina is a characteristic feature of scleral ectasia and pathologic myopia.
rationales.F06: Thinning of the sclera is a common feature of scleral ectasia and pathologic myopia.
rationales.F08: Obliteration of the choroid is a characteristic feature of pathologic myopia and scleral ectasia with choroidal obliteration.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina and the choroid being obliterated, as shown by spectral-domain optical coherence tomography, strongly supports this diagnosis.
